affirmation: A consumer product can be placed on the EU market only if an economic operator established in the Union is responsible for it; without one "the product cannot be placed on the market" (resume; effet.si_non_texte)
citation: A product covered by this Regulation shall not be placed on the market unless there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for the tasks set out in Article 4(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 in respect to that product.
note: Legal act, Article 16(1). The operator can be an EU manufacturer, the importer, an authorised representative or an EU fulfilment service provider (Article 4(2) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020).

affirmation: The operator's contact details must be "on the product, the packaging or an accompanying document" (resume)
citation: The name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, and contact details, including the postal and electronic address, of the economic operator referred to in paragraph 1 shall be indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.
note: Legal act, Article 16(3). The text also allows the parcel, and requires a postal and an electronic address.

affirmation: The question asked to the seller accepts the contact details only "on the product or the packaging" (effet.question)
correction: The contact details may be indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.
citation: shall be indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document
note: The app question is narrower than Article 16(3): a seller who prints the details on the parcel or on a leaflet is compliant but would answer no.

affirmation: Marketplaces have their own control obligations (resume; source.ref "Art. 16 and 22")
citation: providers of online marketplaces shall designate a single point of contact allowing for direct communication, by electronic means, with Member States’ market surveillance authorities in relation to product safety issues
note: Legal act, Article 22(1). Article 22 lists further duties (Safety Gate registration, acting on orders within two working days, listing information).

affirmation: The rule applies from 13 December 2024 (debut)
citation: It shall apply from 13 December 2024. This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
note: Legal act, Article 52.

affirmation: The rule applies to every product, whatever its HS code (sh: "*")
correction: The Regulation does not apply to medicinal products, food, feed, living plants and animals, animal by-products, plant protection products, certain transport equipment, certain aircraft and antiques.
citation: This Regulation does not apply to: (a) medicinal products for human or veterinary use; (b) food; (c) feed;
note: Legal act, Article 2(2). The excluded categories are outside the electronics and toys of the demo, but the "*" scope overstates the text.

affirmation: The rule covers earbuds, headphones, phones and the other listed devices (resume; sh 851830, 851713)
citation: 1.1. handheld mobile phones; 1.2. tablets; 1.3. digital cameras; 1.4. headphones; 1.5. headsets; 1.6. handheld videogame consoles; 1.7. portable speakers; 1.8. e-readers; 1.9. keyboards; 1.10. mice; 1.11. portable navigation systems; 1.12. earbuds; 1.13. laptops.
note: Legal act. The app only maps two HS subheadings (headphones and earbuds, smartphones); the other eleven categories of the list are not covered by the app.

affirmation: The listed devices "must charge through a USB-C port"; "Without a USB-C port, sale prohibited in the EU" (resume; effet.si_non_texte)
correction: The USB Type-C receptacle is required only in so far as the device is capable of being recharged by means of wired charging.
citation: In so far as they are capable of being recharged by means of wired charging, the categories or classes of radio equipment referred to in point 1 of this Part shall: 2.1. be equipped with the USB Type-C receptacle
note: Legal act, Annex Ia, Part I, point 2. A device that only charges wirelessly is not required to have a USB-C port, so the blocking message is too broad. Above 5 V, 3 A or 15 W the device must also support USB Power Delivery (point 3).

affirmation: The device must carry a pictogram showing whether a charger is supplied (resume; effet.question)
citation: is displayed in a graphic form using a user-friendly and easily accessible pictogram as set out in Part III of Annex Ia when such radio equipment is made available to consumers and other end-users. The pictogram shall be printed on the packaging or affixed to the packaging as a sticker.
note: Legal act, new Article 3a(2) of Directive 2014/53/EU. The pictogram goes on the packaging, not on the device. A separate label on charging power is also required (Article 10(8)), which the app does not ask about.

affirmation: The rule applies from 28 December 2024 (debut)
citation: They shall apply those measures from 28 December 2024 for the categories or classes of radio equipment referred to in Part I, points 1.1 to 1.12 of Annex Ia, and from 28 April 2026 for the categories or classes of radio equipment referred to in Part I, point 1.13 of Annex Ia.
note: Legal act, Article 2(1). Laptops (point 1.13) follow from 28 April 2026. As a directive it applies through national transposition measures.

affirmation: The list of devices is in "Annex I, Part I" of Directive (EU) 2022/2380 (source.ref)
correction: The list is in Part I of Annex Ia, which the Annex to Directive (EU) 2022/2380 inserts into Directive 2014/53/EU.
citation: ANNEX Ia SPECIFICATIONS AND INFORMATION RELATING TO CHARGING APPLICABLE TO CERTAIN CATEGORIES OR CLASSES OF RADIO EQUIPMENT
note: Reference error only: Annex I of Directive 2014/53/EU is a different annex (equipment not covered by the Directive).

affirmation: A toy placed on the EU market bears the CE marking (resume)
citation: Toys made available on the market shall bear the CE marking. 2. The CE marking shall be subject to the general principles set out in Article 30 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008.
note: Legal act, Article 16(1).

affirmation: Without CE marking, the toy cannot be sold in the EU (effet.si_non_texte)
citation: Toys not bearing a CE marking or which do not otherwise comply with this Directive may be shown and used at trade fairs and exhibitions, provided that they are accompanied by a sign which clearly indicates that they do not comply with this Directive and that they will not be made available in the Community before being brought into conformity.
note: Legal act, Article 16(4): the only tolerance is display at trade fairs.

affirmation: The toy "comes with an EU declaration of conformity drawn up by the manufacturer" (resume)
correction: The manufacturer draws up an EC declaration of conformity and keeps it for 10 years after the toy has been placed on the market; the Directive does not require it to accompany the toy.
citation: manufacturers shall draw up an EC declaration of conformity, as referred to in Article 15, and affix the CE marking, as set out in Article 17(1). 3. Manufacturers shall keep the technical documentation and the EC declaration of conformity for a period of 10 years after the toy has been placed on the market.
note: Legal act, Article 4(2) and (3). Two errors: the document is named "EC declaration of conformity" in this Directive, and it is kept on file, not supplied with the toy. The app question ("on file") is right, the summary is not.

affirmation: The rule applies from 20 July 2011 (debut)
citation: They shall apply those measures with effect from 20 July 2011.
note: Legal act, Article 54. The chemical requirements of Annex II, Part III applied later, from 20 July 2013 (Article 55).

affirmation: The governing text is Directive 2009/48/EC, Art. 15 to 17 (source.nom; source.ref)
citation: Directive 2009/48/EC is repealed with effect from 1 August 2030. References to the repealed Directive 2009/48/EC shall be construed as references to this Regulation and shall be read in accordance with the correlation table set out in Annex VIII.
note: The Directive is still the applicable text today, but its replacement is already adopted: Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 on the safety of toys applies from 1 August 2030 (Article 56 quoted here). The watch should mention it.

affirmation: The flat duty applies since 1 July 2026 (resume; debut)
citation: From 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028, a customs duty of EUR 3 per item in a consignment the intrinsic value of which does not exceed a total of EUR 150 shall apply instead of the relief eliminated pursuant to Article 1 of this Regulation
note: Legal act: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 of 11 February 2026, Article 2, published in the Official Journal on 18 February 2026 and applicable from 1 July 2026 (Article 4). Not a press release.

affirmation: The amount is a flat EUR 3 (effet.montant: 3; effet.devise: EUR; titre)
citation: a customs duty of EUR 3 per item in a consignment the intrinsic value of which does not exceed a total of EUR 150
note: Legal act, Article 2. The duty is per item, not per shipment: the app must multiply by the number of items.

affirmation: The duty applies "to each distinct item" in the shipment (resume)
note: The Regulation says "per item" and does not define "item" nor use the word "distinct". The idea that identical goods count once comes from the Council press release of 12 December 2025, which a plain HTTP client cannot download (browser check, HTTP 403), so it could not be verified here.

affirmation: The duty concerns shipments "worth less than EUR 150" / "under EUR 150" (resume; effet.valeur_max: 150; effet.libelle)
correction: The duty applies to consignments whose intrinsic value does not exceed a total of EUR 150, so a consignment of exactly EUR 150 is covered.
citation: a simplified temporary tariff treatment based on a single specific customs duty amount per item, without considering the origin of the goods and covering goods in consignments with an intrinsic value not exceeding a total of EUR 150
note: Legal act, recital 6 and Article 2. The threshold is "not exceeding", not "less than", and it is the intrinsic value of the whole consignment.

affirmation: The duty applies "until the permanent regime takes effect" (resume)
correction: The duty applies from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028.
citation: From 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028, a customs duty of EUR 3 per item
note: Legal act, Article 2. Article 3(2) only provides that the Commission may propose an extension if the central IT system is not ready by 1 July 2028.

affirmation: The duty applies to every shipment under the threshold entering the EU (resume; sh: "*"; effet.type taxe_fixe with no condition)
correction: The EUR 3 duty applies only where the import is VAT exempt under Article 143(1), point (ca), of Directive 2006/112/EC (seller using the Import One-Stop Shop) or where the goods are in a postal consignment; other operators pay the normal Common Customs Tariff.
citation: shall apply instead of the relief eliminated pursuant to Article 1 of this Regulation, where: (a) the importation of the goods is exempt from VAT in accordance with Article 143(1), point (ca), of Directive 2006/112/EC; or (b) the goods are in a postal consignment as defined in Article 1, point (24), of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/2446.
note: Legal act, Article 2. Most serious gap for the demo: for a non-IOSS seller using a courier, the app shows EUR 3 where the ordinary tariff rate applies (recital 6).

affirmation: Goods of EU origin are excluded from the duty (origines_exclues: ["UE"])
correction: The flat duty applies without considering the origin of the goods.
citation: without considering the origin of the goods and covering goods in consignments with an intrinsic value not exceeding a total of EUR 150, should apply to all economic operators that have registered for, and make use of, the special scheme
note: Legal act, recital 6. What matters is that the consignment is imported from a third country, not where the goods were made.

affirmation: The official text is the "Council of the EU, agreement of 12 December 2025", a press release (source.nom; source.ref; nature: texte_officiel)
correction: The legal act is Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 of 11 February 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 1186/2009 as regards the elimination of the threshold-based customs duty relief.
citation: COUNCIL REGULATION (EU) 2026/382 of 11 February 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 1186/2009 as regards the elimination of the threshold-based customs duty relief
note: The app still cites the press release of the political agreement. The act has since been adopted and published (OJ L, 2026/382, 18.2.2026); the source should point to it.

affirmation: The exemption ended on 29 August 2025 (resume; debut)
citation: the amendments outlined herein are effective for articles that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on August 29, 2025.
note: Official notice (CBP, Federal Register, 90 FR 42418), not a press release.

affirmation: Shipments of 800 USD or less are no longer exempt, whatever the country of origin (resume)
citation: suspends the duty-free de minimis exemption otherwise authorized under section 321(a)(2)(C) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, for all covered products, regardless of country of origin, valued at $800 or less
note: Official notice, SUMMARY.

affirmation: "Duties are due from the first dollar" (resume)
citation: regardless of value, country of origin, mode of transportation, or method of entry, that is entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on August 29, 2025. Accordingly, all such shipments, except those sent through the international postal network, shall be subject to all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges.
note: Official notice, section A. "Applicable duties" means the ordinary tariff of the product, which can be zero for some headings. Postal shipments follow a separate duty regime.

affirmation: "No exemption: duties due on every shipment" (effet.texte)
correction: The de minimis exemption continues to apply to the donations and informational materials covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), and postal shipments are charged under a separate duty regime.
citation: The de minimis exemption shall continue to apply to such donations and informational materials in accordance with section 2(a) of Executive Order 14324 and the HTSUS modifications as set forth in the Annex to this document.
note: Official notice, section F. Not relevant to commercial electronics, but "every shipment" is too absolute.

affirmation: The source is Executive Order 14324, implemented by CBP, Federal Register 2025-16802 (source.nom; source.ref)
citation: In order to effectuate the President's Executive Order 14324 of July 30, 2025 (Suspending Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment For All Countries), the Secretary of Homeland Security has determined that appropriate action is needed to ensure collection of applicable duties
note: Document number 2025-16802 read on the page itself.

affirmation: The 2025 notice is presented as the text in force today (nature: texte_officiel; source)
correction: Executive Order 14324 was revised by Executive Order 14388 of 20 February 2026, and CBP wrote an indefinite suspension of the exemption into its regulations by an interim final rule effective on 24 June 2026.
citation: This document amends the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations to implement an indefinite suspension of the de minimis administrative exemption for imports valued at $800 or less arriving via all modes other than through the international postal network.
note: Official interim final rule (91 FR 37789, document 2026-12670). The rule itself is unchanged for the demo (no exemption at or under $800), but the cited source is outdated: the Supreme Court ruling of 20 February 2026 on IEEPA tariffs led to Executive Order 14388 (91 FR 9433), then to this rule. The watch should cite it.

affirmation: The importer of a children's product certifies in writing that it complies, based on testing by a third-party laboratory accepted by the CPSC (resume; effet.question; source.nom)
citation: requires domestic manufacturers and importers of children’s products to certify in a written Children’s Product Certificate (CPC), based on test results from a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory
note: Regulator page (CPSC), which itself cites section 14 of the CPSA and 16 CFR part 1110. The same page announces that from 8 July 2026 importers must also file certificates electronically with CBP (eFiling); the app does not mention it.

affirmation: The rule is applied to toys only (sh: 9503)
correction: The certificate is required for any children's product, meaning a consumer product designed or intended primarily for children 12 years of age or younger, that is subject to a children's product safety rule.
citation: a consumer product designed or intended primarily for children 12 years of age or younger, that are subject to a consumer product safety rule, or a similar ban, standard, or regulation under any other CPSC-enforced statute (children’s product safety rules), require third-party testing and certification.
note: Regulator page. The app scope is narrower than the rule: children's clothing, nursery products or children's electronics outside heading 9503 also need a CPC.

affirmation: The obligation started on 14 August 2008 (debut)
correction: 14 August 2008 is the date of enactment of Public Law 110-314; third-party testing and certification apply to a children's product manufactured more than 90 days after the Commission published the accreditation requirements for the safety rule concerned.
citation: the requirements of paragraph (2) shall apply to any children's product manufactured more than 90 days after the Commission has established and published notice of the requirements for accreditation of third party conformity assessment bodies to assess conformity with a children's product safety rule to which such children's product is subject.
note: Statute, 15 U.S.C. 2063(a)(3)(A) (2023 edition of the US Code on govinfo). The start date therefore differs by safety rule; no single date can be stated from the text.

affirmation: "Without a CPC, CBP can refuse the import" (effet.si_non_texte)
citation: shall be refused admission into such customs territory if such product (1) fails to comply with an applicable consumer product safety rule; (2) is not accompanied by a certificate required by this chapter or any other Act enforced by the Commission
note: Statute, 15 U.S.C. 2066(a). The text is stronger than the app: the product "shall be refused admission". The statute does not name CBP. In the source a dash follows the word "product"; it is left out of the quotation because the checker reads that HTML entity as a space.

affirmation: A device that emits radio waves must have an FCC equipment authorization before it is imported or marketed in the United States (resume; source.nom "47 CFR part 2, subpart J")
citation: Radio Frequency (RF) devices are required to be properly authorized under 47 CFR part 2 prior to being marketed or imported into the United States.
note: Regulator page (FCC, Office of Engineering and Technology). The page adds "with certain limited exceptions".

affirmation: An FCC identifier (FCC ID) or a supplier's declaration of conformity is enough for a Bluetooth or Wi-Fi device (effet.question)
correction: Intentional radiators operating under part 15, which is the case of Bluetooth and Wi-Fi transmitters, must be certified; the Supplier's Declaration of Conformity is limited to the few categories listed in 47 CFR 15.201(a).
citation: all intentional radiators operating under the provisions of this part shall be certified by the Telecommunication Certification Bodies pursuant to the procedures in subpart J of part 2 of this chapter prior to marketing.
note: Regulation, 47 CFR 15.201(b) (edition of 1 October 2024 on govinfo). For the earbuds of the demo, a seller holding only a declaration of conformity would wrongly pass the app check.

affirmation: "Without FCC authorization, import prohibited" (effet.si_non_texte)
citation: Radio frequency devices may be imported only if one or more of these conditions are met: (1) The radio frequency device has been issued an equipment authorization by the FCC.
note: Regulation, 47 CFR 2.1204(a). The same paragraph lists other conditions that allow import without authorization (testing samples, trade shows, export only, three or fewer devices for personal use); none fits a commercial sale.

affirmation: The rule started on 1 October 1998 (debut)
note: No date of 1 October 1998 appears on the FCC equipment authorization page nor in the sections of 47 CFR part 2 and part 15 that were read. Origin of this date unknown.

affirmation: Lithium-ion power banks fall within the scope of the law "since 1 February 2019" (resume; debut)
correction: Power banks have been regulated since 1 February 2018; a one-year transitional period ran until 31 January 2019, after which unmarked stock can no longer be sold.
citation: 平成３０年２月１日以降、製造、輸入又は販売の事業を行う者は、ＰＳＥマーク表示の無いモバイルバッテリーを販売することはできない（流通在庫を含む）。ただし、事業者における対応の準備期間として平成３１年１月３１日までの１年間を経過措置期間とし、この間は、これまでの扱いによることもできる。
note: Regulator page (METI FAQ on mobile batteries, answer 14, in Japanese; Heisei 30 is 2018 and Heisei 31 is 2019). The METI guide cited by the app does not mention power banks or this date at all.

affirmation: All lithium-ion power banks are covered (resume; sh 850760)
correction: Only power banks whose cells have a volumetric energy density of 400 Wh/L or more per cell are covered.
citation: A.1 内蔵する単電池１個当たりの体積エネルギー密度が、400Wh/L（ワット時毎リットル）以上のものが対象となる。なお、エネルギー密度の算出方法については、通達
note: Regulator page (METI FAQ, answer 1, in Japanese). In practice most power banks exceed this density, but the limit exists. The FAQ also excludes portable power stations with AC output (answer 4).

affirmation: "Manufacture, import and sale are prohibited without technical conformity and PSE marking"; "Without PSE marking, import and sale prohibited in Japan" (resume; effet.si_non_texte)
correction: What the Act prohibits without correct PSE marking is selling or displaying for sale; manufacturers and importers must notify their business and ensure conformity to the technical requirements.
citation: It is stipulated in Article 27 of the Act, if the PSE mark or the name of the notifying supplier is not displayed correctly, the sellers must not sell or display for sale the Electrical appliance and Materials.
note: METI guide, section 7 (Article 27 of the Act). The guide states that it is an unofficial translation and that only the Japanese texts have legal effect. The name of the notifying supplier must appear next to the mark.

affirmation: An importer must be declared to METI (effet.question; effet.si_oui)
citation: Persons engaged in manufacturing or importing products that fall under Electrical Appliances and Materials must, within 30 days from the commencement of such business, notify the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry of such business.
note: METI guide, section 1.1.3 (Articles 3 to 6 of the Act). The notifying importer must be a business in Japan; the guide is an unofficial translation.

affirmation: AC adapters are also covered (resume; sh 850440)
citation: the AC/DC adapter (including the connector that comes with the AC/DC adapter) is classified as the category of Electrical Appliances and Materials, but the smartphone is not classified as this category.
note: METI guide, footnote 1. Figure 1 of the same guide lists the AC adapter among the Specified items, which need a conformity assessment by a registered body and the diamond PSE mark, whereas lithium-ion batteries are Non-Specified (round mark). The app treats both alike.

affirmation: The rule concerns goods with a customs value of 1,000 AUD or less (resume; effet.texte)
citation: If you are a non-resident business and you sell goods into Australia with a customs value of A$1,000 or less, GST applies and you will have to collect this from your customer and send the GST to us.
note: Regulator page (ATO, last updated 11 September 2025). Exception stated on the page: several low value goods shipped as one consignment worth over A$1,000 are taxed at the border instead.

affirmation: The goods are "sold to an Australian consumer" (resume)
citation: low value goods imported into Australia with a customs value of A$1,000 or less when the price is first agreed with the consumer
note: Regulator page (ATO, How Australian GST works). Sales to GST-registered Australian businesses are not concerned.

affirmation: The GST rate is 10% (resume; effet.texte)
citation: The GST rate in Australia is 10%, meaning GST is 1/11th of the amount you charge for sales connected with Australia.
note: Regulator page (ATO).

affirmation: The GST is collected at the point of sale by the seller or by the marketplace (resume)
citation: Only one business is required to charge GST on a sale: If an EDP operator is responsible for GST on a sale, the merchant won't be responsible for GST.
note: Regulator page (ATO). EDP means electronic distribution platform, the marketplace; a redeliverer can also be the liable party.

affirmation: The rule applies since 1 July 2018 (debut)
citation: This applied from 1 July 2018 and applies to sales of: individual low value imported goods multiple low value imported goods.
note: Regulator page (ATO).

affirmation: "10% GST to collect at the point of sale" for every seller (effet.texte, no condition)
correction: A non-resident seller must register and charge GST only if its GST turnover from sales connected with Australia is equal to or greater than A$75,000 (A$150,000 for a non-profit organisation).
citation: Your GST turnover from sales connected with Australia from your enterprise is equal to, or greater than the registration turnover threshold of A$75,000 (or A$150,000 if you are a non-profit organisation).
note: Regulator page (ATO, How Australian GST works). Below the threshold the seller does not collect GST, unless it registers voluntarily or sells through a marketplace that is liable.

affirmation: The standard applies since 22 June 2022 (resume; debut)
citation: The mandatory safety standard applies to all new and second-hand items supplied on or after 22 June 2022, unless the supply is a one-off private transaction by a consumer such as a private sale.
note: Regulator page (ACCC Product Safety). The legal instrument is the Consumer Goods (Products Containing Button/Coin Batteries) Safety Standard 2020, not read here.

affirmation: A consumer product containing button or coin batteries must have a secure compartment (resume; effet.question)
citation: Consumer goods containing button and coin batteries must have a secure battery compartment.
note: Regulator page. The detail on the same page: the child-resistant compartment is required where the batteries are intended to be user-replaceable, and in every case the goods must not release the batteries during use or misuse.

affirmation: The product must have passed the tests set by the mandatory standard (resume; effet.question)
citation: You must demonstrate that products containing button and coin batteries comply with the mandatory safety standard prior to supply to consumers.
note: Regulator page. Testing may follow a product-specific or a non-product-specific industry standard.

affirmation: The rule is applied to toys and clocks only (sh: 9503, 9105)
correction: The standard applies to all consumer goods containing, or intended to contain, button and coin batteries, with exclusions for hearing aids, certain professional equipment and audio-visual or ICT equipment whose batteries are soldered in place.
citation: This mandatory safety standard applies to consumer goods containing, or intended to contain, button and coin batteries, including: cameras or calculators toys, games, novelty items and musical greeting cards
note: Regulator page. Remote controls, scales, thermometers, key fobs or earbud cases with a coin cell are in scope but outside the two HS headings of the app.

affirmation: "Unsecured button batteries: sale prohibited in Australia" (effet.si_non_texte)
citation: Suppliers must make sure that consumer goods and accessories containing button and coin batteries: have a secure battery compartment pass compliance testing.
note: Regulator page, which also states that fines and penalties may apply and that a recall may be needed. The prohibition on supplying non-compliant goods comes from the Australian Consumer Law, which was not read here. Three other mandatory standards (warnings and packaging) exist and are not in the app.

affirmation: Lithium-ion batteries shipped alone (UN 3480) are forbidden on passenger aircraft: cargo aircraft only, with prescribed labelling (resume)
citation: All lithium-ion cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3480) are forbidden for transport as cargo on passenger aircraft. All packages prepared in accordance with Packing Instruction 965, Section IA and IB, must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label, in addition to other required marks and/or labels.
note: Public IATA Battery Guidance Document, revised for the 2026 Regulations (PDF linked from the IATA batteries page). It is guidance, not the Dangerous Goods Regulations themselves, which are behind a paywall. Exception: carriage on a passenger aircraft is possible with authority approval under Special Provision A201.

affirmation: State of charge of 30% at most, under Packing Instruction 965 (resume; source.ref; effet.question)
citation: must be shipped at a state of charge (SoC) not exceeding 30% of their rated capacity. Cells and/or batteries at a SoC of greater than 30% may only be shipped with the approval of the State of Origin and the State of the Operator in accordance with Special Provision A331
note: Public IATA guidance document. The same document states that from 1 January 2026 the 30% limit also applies to lithium-ion batteries packed with equipment (PI 966), which the app does not cover.

affirmation: The rule applies since 1 April 2016 (debut)
note: Neither the public IATA batteries page nor the 2026 guidance document gives this date. The ICAO news page that would state it refuses plain HTTP clients (HTTP 403), and the Dangerous Goods Regulations are behind a paywall.

affirmation: The 30% limit and the UN 3480 label also condition shipment "by land or sea" (effet.question)
note: The IATA document only covers air transport. Nothing read supports a 30% state of charge requirement for road or sea carriage.

affirmation: "Transport refused by the carrier" if the conditions are not met (effet.si_non_texte)
note: The public guidance does not describe carrier refusal. It states that shipment above 30% state of charge, or on a passenger aircraft, remains possible with State approvals (Special Provisions A331 and A201).

affirmation: The rule applies in every jurisdiction (juridictions: ["*"])
note: The public IATA pages read do not state the geographic or legal reach of the Dangerous Goods Regulations. The guidance document says it is based on the ICAO Technical Instructions and "should not be relied upon as a source of regulatory compliance".
